problem: "every XML attribute has a setter" is false and contradicts what the rest of the chapter teaches. Layout attributes such as android:layout_width, android:layout_weight and android:layout_margin map to fields on the parent's LayoutParams, not to setters on the view (there is no setWeight). Some attributes, like android:onClick or android:style, are read by the framework during inflation and have no matching public setter. A student reading this will hunt for calls that do not exist.
fix: Write: most view attributes map to a setter, for example android:text → setText and android:visibility → setVisibility. Attributes that start with layout_ do not: they belong to the parent's LayoutParams, so you set them with new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(...) or by calling setLayoutParams.

where: Section 1 note and Exam traps (first trap), repeated in Quiz Q2
problem: "addView(view) alone falls back to wrap_content" is not always true. addView with no params uses the parent's generateDefaultLayoutParams(). For a vertical LinearLayout that is MATCH_PARENT width × WRAP_CONTENT height, so the width is not wrap_content. Only the horizontal case gives wrap_content in both directions. The main point (weight is ignored) is right, the detail is not.
fix: Say: without params the parent uses its default LayoutParams, which for LinearLayout is wrap_content × wrap_content when horizontal and match_parent × wrap_content when vertical. Weight can only be set through an explicit LinearLayout.LayoutParams, so it silently does nothing here.

problem: The example says "Build a horizontal LinearLayout in code", but the shown code never creates a LinearLayout, a Button, LayoutParams, an id or an OnClickListener. It is only integer arithmetic in a main method, so the reader never sees the API calls the example claims to demonstrate.
fix: Either add the real lines (LinearLayout root = new LinearLayout(this); root.setOrientation(LinearLayout.HORIZONTAL); Button b = new Button(this); b.setId(100 + i); b.setLayoutParams(new LinearLayout.LayoutParams(0, LinearLayout.LayoutParams.WRAP_CONTENT, 1f)); root.addView(b); b.setOnClickListener(listener); setContentView(root)), or state clearly that the snippet only does the width arithmetic and that the layout calls are shown in Section 1.
